name: Hon Da Bac
kicker: Granite on the Gulf, west of the city
summary: Three granite rocks on the Gulf of Thailand, about 6.43 hectares, the highest about 50 meters. Walk the causeway to Hòn Đá Bạc, with Hòn Ông Ngộ and Hòn Đá Lẻ beside it, and see the whale skeleton at Lăng Ông Nam Hải. The national extract prints no fee. Two tour pages print 20,000 VND for an adult and 10,000 VND for a child. One tour page prints 07:00–19:00. The relic page prints no clock. Check on arrival.
getThere: About 50 km by water and 42 km by road on the national extract. The airline guide says about 50 km.

body: Walk out to the granite. The national tourism extract describes about 6.43 hectares and three rocks, Hòn Ông Ngộ, Hòn Đá Lẻ, and Hòn Đá Bạc, the highest about 50 meters, and shapes it calls sân tiên, giếng tiên, bàn chân tiên, and bàn tay tiên. The same extract names Lăng Ông Nam Hải, a whale skeleton, and the 7 December 1971 fight over a 105 mm gun position. UNESCO includes the rock in the biosphere’s offshore groups.

The relic page dates the national listing to Decision 2245/QĐ-BVHTTDL on 22 June 2009, under the name Hòn Đá Bạc – Trung tâm chỉ huy kế hoạch phản gián CM12, 9 September 1981–9 September 1984. It also names a victory monument, a tradition house, and a Bác Hồ temple on the site. This is not the melaleuca gate at U Minh Hạ, even where both pages use xã Đá Bạc.

The extract puts the rock at xóm Kinh Hòn, xã Khánh Bình Tây, huyện Trần Văn Thời. The relic page says ấp Kênh Hòn, xã Đá Bạc. The road the extract describes goes toward U Minh Hạ, then Nông trường Minh Hà, Cơi Năm, and ấp Đá Bạc B, then one bridge onto the rock. Tour pages name the drier months, December to April. The relic page prints no season.
